blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Pretrained video models learn associations between language descriptions, visual content, and visual dynamics, acquiring visual and dynamics priors across scenes, objects, and interactions [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] . These experiences provide a foundation for robots to understand manipulation goals and predict environmental changes [ 5 , 6 ] . World action models (WAMs) jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language, connecting visual changes to robot actions and providing a route from video pretraining to robot control [ 7 , 8 ] . This paper studies how to better use these priors to extend language-conditioned video modeling into generalizable action capabilities.
blocks.zh: 预受训练的视频模型学习语言描述,视觉内容,和视觉动态之间的关联,获得跨场景,对象的视觉和动态前传,以及互动[1,2,3,4]. 这些经验为机器人理解操纵目标并预测环境变化提供了基础[5,6]. 世界行动模型(WAMS)联合预测以语言为条件的视频和行动,将视觉变化与机器人动作连接起来,并提供从视频预训到机器人控制的路线[7,8]. 本文研究如何更好地利用这些前科,将语言条件化的视频模型扩展为通俗化的动作能力.

blocks.en:
When we introduce action prediction, the language–video capabilities acquired in video pretraining should be preserved.
This requires further alignment between language, video, and action.
It bridges the gap between language-described targets, visual observation, and executed actions.
Existing work on WAMs largely focused on model architectures and training mechanisms [ 9 , 10 ] .
Methods on video pretraining often treat the language–video alignment as an established foundation [ 7 , 8 ] .
However, introducing action learning raises a basic question: how to preserve established language–video prior and further solve language–video–action misalignment?
The roles of different experiences and forms of supervision in this process, particularly for control generalization, remain unclear [ 9 , 10 , 11 , 12 ] .
blocks.zh:
当我们引入动作预测时,应该保留在视频预训中获得的语言-视频能力.
这需要进一步协调语言、视频和行动。
它弥合了语言描述的目标、视觉观察和执行行动之间的差距。
关于WAM的现有工作主要侧重于示范架构和培训机制[9,10].
视频预训方法往往将语言-视频对接作为既定的基础[7,8].
然而,引入行动学习提出了一个基本问题:如何保留既定的语言-视频先发制人,并进一步解决语言-视频-行动错位?
不同经验和监督形式在这一过程中的作用,特别是在控制一般化方面的作用,仍然不明确[9、10、11、12]。

blocks.en:
To study these questions, we first construct a multisource data pool with approximately 47,000 hours, comprising approximately 11,000 hours of general videos, 11,000 hours of egocentric videos, 15,000 hours of in-house UMI demonstrations, and 10,000 hours of robot demonstrations, as shown in Figure 2 (a) .
These sources provide different forms of cross-modal supervision.
General and egocentric videos primarily provide language–video supervision, covering general visual dynamics and human interactions, respectively.
UMI demonstrations record video and action trajectories of humans manipulating objects with handheld grippers, while robot demonstrations provide observations, states, and actions during robot task execution.
Both include language descriptions corresponding to the manipulation process, supporting language–video–action learning in addition to language–video supervision.
UMI demonstrations provide scalable human manipulation experience, whereas robot demonstrations provide direct but more limited robot control experience [ 13 , 14 , 15 ] . The sources differ in scene and task coverage and in the completeness of language and action supervision. Multisource pretraining therefore requires combining these experiences appropriately: language–video supervision preserves video pretraining capabilities, while human and robot action supervision establishes video–action correspondences [ 16 , 17 , 18 ] .
blocks.zh:
为了研究这些问题,我们首先构建了一个大约47 000小时的多源数据库,其中包括大约11 000小时的一般录像、11 000小时的自我中心录像、15 000小时的内部UMI演示和10 000小时的机器人演示,如图2(a)所示。
这些来源提供了不同形式的跨模式监管.
一般和以自我为中心的视频主要提供语言-视频监督,分别涵盖一般视觉动态和人际互动.
UMI演示记录了人类用手持抓取器操纵物体的视频和行动轨迹,而机器人演示则在机器人任务执行期间提供观察,状态,和行动.
两者都包含与操控过程相适应的语言描述,除了语言-视频监督之外,还支持语言-视频-动作学习.
UMI演示提供了可扩展的人类操纵经验,而机器人演示则提供了直接但更有限的机器人控制经验[13,14,15]. 信息来源在现场和任务覆盖面以及语言和行动监督的完整性方面各不相同。 因此,多源预训需要适当地综合这些经验:语言-视频监督保留视频预训能力,而人和机器人行动监督则建立视频-行动通信[16,17,18].

blocks.en:
Building on the constructed multisource experience, we conduct systematic studies at three levels: language–video alignment, language–video–action alignment, and joint learning.
Specifically, at the language–video level, we examine how to preserve the visual prior in pretrained video generation with the design of language supervision.
At the language–video–action level, we investigate how to utilize action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations to help action prediction and robot control.
In joint training, we study the data recipe and model architecture for better cross-modality modeling.
The data recipe determines the coverage of the visual and interaction experience in tasks, scenes, and the proportions of different experiences.
The model architecture answers how to conduct cross-modal supervision through modality interactions and language conditioning pathways, as shown in Figure 2 (b) .
We further examine the benefits of scaling training with the resulting data and supervision recipe.
blocks.zh:
基于构建的多来源经验,我们在三个层面进行系统研究:语言-视频对接,语言-视频对接,以及联合学习。
具体地说,在语言视频层面,我们研究如何通过设计语言监督,在预先训练的视频生成中保留视觉。
在语言-视频-动作层面,我们调查如何利用UMI和机器人演示的动作监督来帮助动作预测和机器人控制.
在联合培训中,我们研究数据配方和模型结构,以更好地建立跨模式模型。
数据配方决定了任务,场景中视觉和互动体验的覆盖范围,以及不同体验的比例.
如图2(b)所示,示范架构通过模式互动和语言调节路径,解决如何进行跨模式监督的问题。
我们进一步审查利用由此产生的数据和监督方法扩大培训的效益。

blocks.en:
Our study shows that preserving language–video capabilities and extending language–video–action capabilities jointly support control generalization in WAMs.
Detailed manipulation descriptions and environmental cues improve language–video supervision, which maintains language–video alignment and thereby improves control generalization.
And UMI demonstrations improve robot control in simulation and real scenes, proving the value of human manipulation experience with action supervision for robot learning.
In joint learning, the benefits of multisource experience depend both on data and model supervision recipe.
Experiments show that increasing training investment under the selected data and model recipe further improves control generalization.
These findings provide empirical guidance for data collection and organization, supervision design, and joint training in WAMs. The pretraining recipe derived from these findings achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under the RoboTwin Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) settings, respectively. Ours achieves 40.00% SR under the Hard setting across three real-world tasks, exceeding OpenWAM’s 23.33%. This result indicates better generalization to unseen objects and backgrounds.
blocks.zh:
我们的研究表明,保留语言-视频能力和扩展语言-视频-行动能力共同支持WAMs的控制通论.
详细的操纵描述和环境提示改进了语言-视频监督,它维持了语言-视频对齐,从而改进了控制通俗化.
而UMI演示则改进了模拟和真实场景中的机器人控制,证明了人类操纵经验对机器人学习的动作监督的价值.
在联合学习中,多来源经验的好处既取决于数据,也取决于模型监督方法。
实验显示,在选定的数据和模型配方下增加培训投资会进一步改善控制通俗化.
这些结论为数据收集和组织、监督设计以及WAM联合培训提供了经验指导。 根据这些调查结果得出的预训方法,在RoboTwin Easy(从清到清)和Hard(从清到地)的环境下,成功率分别为88.10%和61.56%。 超过OpenWAM的23.33%。 这一结果表明,对看不见的物体和背景作了更好的概括。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: World Action Models. World action models aim to connect visual observations with executable robot actions [ 7 ] . Early work treated video as a transferable visual plan or dynamic representation. UniPi first generates a language-conditioned visual plan and then recovers actions with an inverse-dynamics module [ 19 ] . VPP conditions a policy on predictive representations from a video model [ 6 ] . Motus, DreamZero, and LingBot-VA place visual dynamics and action prediction within unified or interactive architectures, exploring discrete tokens, latent actions, joint flow matching, and causal video–action modeling [ 20 , 7 , 8 ] . Fast-WAM and InternW0- Δ \Delta further distinguish future supervision during training from action generation at inference, showing that the prediction target and the deployment interface can be separated [ 21 , 17 ] . VPP2 and LingBot-VA adapt video pretraining to robot manipulation by studying how manipulation data organization, temporal and video representation modeling, and action-branch adaptation can preserve video prediction capabilities while supporting action learning [ 18 , 8 ] . We build on this foundation and focus on how language–video capabilities from video pretraining can transfer to language–video–action learning and action control.
blocks.zh: 世界行动模式。 世界行动模型旨在将视觉观测与可执行的机器人动作相接 [7]. 早期的工作将视频视为可转移的视觉计划或动态表现. UniPi首先生成一个语言条件的视觉计划,再用反向动力学模块恢复动作[19]. VPP以视频模型的预测表示政策为条件[6]. Motus, DreamZero和LingBot-VA将视觉动态和行动预测置于统一或互动的架构中,探索离散的符号,潜伏的动作,联合流相匹配,以及因果视频-行动模型[20, 7, 8]. Fast-WAM和InternW0-\\Delta在推论中进一步区分了未来训练期间的监督与动作生成,表明预测目标和部署接口可以分开[21,17]. VPP2和LingBot-VA通过研究操纵数据组织,时间和视频表现模型,以及动作分支适应如何在支持动作学习的同时保留视频预测能力来使视频预训适应机器人操纵. [18, 8]. 我们以此为基础,关注从视频预训中语言-视频能力如何转移到语言-视频-动作学习和动作控制。

blocks.en: Multisource Data for Robot Learning. Robot learning increasingly draws on cross-embodiment trajectories, general videos, egocentric videos, and human manipulation demonstrations rather than a single source of robot data. Open X-Embodiment, Octo, and OpenVLA aggregate and filter multi-robot data to study shared representations, observation adaptation, and action-space alignment, showing that cross-embodiment learning requires source normalization and interface alignment [ 22 , 23 , 24 ] . General and egocentric videos expand coverage of scenes, objects, and interaction dynamics, but usually lack action labels directly corresponding to robot execution [ 25 , 26 ] . EgoMimic and EgoScale study how such human experience can be transferred through view and embodiment alignment, including settings with limited robot data [ 27 , 28 ] . UMI complements these sources by using portable interfaces to record manipulation trajectories in an end-effector-like interaction format, thereby providing action supervision associated with the manipulation process [ 13 , 14 , 15 ] . EgoWAM, Ego4WAM, and Motus further demonstrate the complementary roles of video, action trajectories, semantic descriptions, and world-prediction targets [ 29 , 10 , 20 ] . The central issue in multisource learning is therefore not simply adding sources, but understanding differences in scene coverage, interaction dynamics, embodiment interfaces, and available supervision. We curate approximately 47,000 hours of multisource data. We use this pool to systematically examine how experience combinations and supervision design affect WAM pretraining.
blocks.zh: 机器人学习多源数据. 机器人学习越来越多地取材于交叉表现的轨迹,一般视频,以自我为中心的视频,以及人类操纵演示,而不是机器人数据的一个单一来源. 开放X-Embodiment,Octo,和OpenVLA对多机器人数据进行汇总和过滤,以研究共享的表示,观测适应,以及动作-空间相接,显示交叉化学习需要源常态化和界面相接[22,23,24]. 一般和以自我为中心的视频扩大了场景,物体,互动动态的覆盖范围,但通常缺乏与机器人执行直接对应的动作标签[25,26]. EgoMimic和EgoScale研究这种人类经验如何通过取景和化身相接,包括有限的机器人数据设置[27,28]. UMI通过使用便携式接口来以类似终端效应的交互格式记录操纵轨迹来补充这些来源,从而提供与操纵过程相相联的动作监督[13,14,15]. EgoWAM,Ego4WAM,和Motus进一步展示了视频,动作轨迹,语义描述以及世界预测目标[29,10,20]等互补作用. 因此,多来源学习的中心问题不仅仅是增加来源,而是理解场景覆盖、互动动态、浮雕界面和可用监督方面的差异。 我们掌握了大约47 000小时的多来源数据。 我们利用这个集合系统审查经验组合和监督设计如何影响WAM预训.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: This section presents the world action model and its multimodal supervision. We first present the problem formulation, model architecture, and training objectives, then describe multisource experience curation and supervision construction. Pretraining uses four types of experience: general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. These sources differ in scene and task distributions, data quality, manipulation diversity, and available action supervision. General and egocentric videos provide language–video supervision, while UMI and robot demonstrations additionally provide state and action signals where available and valid. In Table 2 and Figure 2 , we summarize the composition, scale, and video-duration distribution of the pretraining pool after data curation and cleaning.

blocks.en: Control learning primarily supervised by observation–action pairs must jointly address scene understanding, interaction dynamics, and action generation. We adopt a world action model (WAM) based on a pretrained video model, using the associations between language descriptions and visual dynamics learned during video pretraining and learning correspondences between manipulation processes and executed actions through action supervision. The model jointly predicts video changes and actions over the same interval. The video sequence V n : n + K V_{n:n+K} describes observable scene evolution during manipulation, while the action sequence A n : n + K A_{n:n+K} describes the corresponding manipulation behavior. The two sequences span the same physical time interval but may use different sampling rates.
blocks.zh: 控制学习主要由观察-行动对子监督,必须共同解决现场理解、互动动态和动作生成问题。 我们采用了基于预先训练的视频模型的世界行动模式(WAM),利用在视频预训中学习的语言描述和视觉动态之间的关联,学习操纵过程之间的对应关系,并通过行动监督执行行动. 该模型共同预测视频变化和动作在同一间隔. 视频序列 Vn:n + K V_{n:n+K }描述在操纵过程中可观察到的场景演化,而动作序列 An:n + K A_{n:n+K }则描述相应的操纵行为. 这两个序列跨越相同的物理时间间隔,但可能使用不同的取样率。

blocks.en: The final equality follows from our modeling choice that the video branch is not conditioned on the proprioceptive state. The first term learns language-conditioned video prediction, corresponding to language–video learning. The second term predicts actions from language, video information, and the current state. Together, the two terms constitute joint language–video–action learning.
blocks.zh: 最终的平等源于我们的模特选择 视频分支不以自制状态为条件 第一个术语学习语言条件的视频预测,对应语言-视频学习. 第二个术语从语言,视频信息,以及当前状态来预测动作. 这两个术语共同构成联合语言-视频-行动学习。

blocks.en: Starting from a pretrained video model, we train a unified WAM end to end with a joint prediction objective. The action branch uses visual dynamics and language conditioning information supplied by the video branch. Training retains the video prediction objective while introducing action supervision, aiming to continue using existing language–video modeling capabilities and to learn correspondences between manipulation processes in video and executed actions.
blocks.zh: 从一个经过预先训练的视频模型开始,我们训练一个统一的WAM端以联合预测目标结束. 动作分会使用视频分会提供的视觉动态和语言调节信息. 培训保留了视频预测目标,同时引入了行动监督,目的是继续利用现有语言-视频模拟能力,并学习视频操作过程与执行行动之间的对应。

blocks.en: Multisource experience supplies different parts of the supervision for joint prediction. General and egocentric videos provide language–video correspondences for learning language-conditioned visual dynamics. UMI and robot demonstrations additionally provide actions temporally associated with video, enabling action prediction alongside video learning. All samples participate in video learning. Samples with valid action annotations additionally participate in action learning. Missing or invalid action targets contribute no action supervision. Experiences with different supervision coverage can therefore participate in unified WAM pretraining.
blocks.zh: 多源经验为联合预测提供了监督的不同部分. 以一般和自我为中心的视频为学习语言条件的视觉动态提供语言-视频通信。 UMI和机器人演示还提供了与视频时间相关的动作,使动作预测与视频学习同时进行. 所有样本都参与视频学习. 附有有效行动说明的样本还参与行动学习。 缺少或无效的行动目标无助于行动监督。 因此,不同监督范围的经验可以参加WAM统一预训.

blocks.en: We illustrate the model architecture and the attention masks used during training and inference in Figure 3 . The model uses a MoT architecture [ 30 ] , with the video branch initialized from Wan [ 2 ] and the action branch randomly initialized. The action DiT branch comprises action and state encoders, transformer blocks, and an action decoder. Video and action maintain separate residual streams, with joint attention passing information unidirectionally from video to action. The video token stream passes through the video branch and causally attends to current and past video tokens. The action token stream passes through the action branch and attends to video tokens from past and current chunks, as well as state and action tokens within the current chunk. This unidirectional interaction allows samples with video supervision alone to continue training the video branch without directly updating the action branch through the video objective, supporting the use of videos without action supervision.
blocks.zh: 我们在图3中说明了在培训和推论期间使用的模型结构和注意口罩。 该模型使用MOT架构[30],视频分支从Wan[2]初始化,动作分支随机初始化. 动作DiT分支由动作和状态编码器,变压器块和一个动作解码器组成. 视频和行动保持单独的剩余流,共同关注将信息从视频单向传递到行动。 视频信使流通过视频分支,并因果关注当前和过去的视频信使. 动作符流通过动作分支,并关注过去和当前块的视频符,以及当前块内的状态和动作符. 这种单向互动让仅拥有视频监督的样本能够继续培训视频分支,而无需通过视频目标直接更新动作分支,支持使用视频而无需行动监督.

blocks.en: The video branch receives encoded language conditions through cross-attention. The action branch uses language information only through attention interactions with the video branch and has no direct text cross-attention. This conditioning pathway aims to reuse the language–video correspondences established during video pretraining, allowing action prediction to use semantic information associated with the manipulation process. The video branch predicts flow velocities in video latent space, while the action branch decodes its output tokens into flow velocities in action space.
blocks.zh: 视频分支通过交叉调取接收被编码的语言条件. 动作分支仅通过与视频分支的注意力互动而使用语言信息,没有直接的文本交叉关注. 这种调制路径旨在重用在视频预训期间建立的语言-视频通信,使动作预测能够使用与操纵过程相关的语义信息. 视频分会预测视频潜伏空间中的流速,而动作分会将输出符解码为动作空间中的流速.

blocks.en: General videos. We use OpenVid [ 32 ] and Panda70M [ 33 ] , totaling 10,909.6 hours. These open-source video generation datasets contain videos and text descriptions covering diverse scenes, objects, and visual dynamics. We retain their videos and original descriptions to provide language–video experience beyond manipulation demonstrations.
blocks.zh: 一般视频. 使用OpenVid [32]和Panda70M [33],共计10,909.6小时. 这些开源视频生成数据集包含视频和文本描述,涵盖了不同的场景,物体,和视觉动态. 我们保留了他们的视频和原始描述,以提供语言的视频体验,而不是操控示威。

blocks.en: Egocentric videos. We use Ego4D [ 25 ] , EgoVerse [ 26 ] , and EgoSuite [ 34 ] , totaling 371,212 trajectories and 10,986.3 hours. Ego4D primarily records daily activities across real-life settings. EgoVerse covers more diverse scenes, adding egocentric visual experience across environments. EgoSuite is currently the largest open-source egocentric manipulation video dataset. We retain the videos and language descriptions from these sources.
blocks.zh: 爱果心视频. 我们使用"Ego4D"[25],"EgoVerse"[26],"EgoSuite"[34],共371,212个出轨和10,986.3小时. Ego4D主要记录现实生活中的日常活动. EgoVerse覆盖了更多样化的场景,增加了以自负为中心的各种环境的视觉体验. EgoSuite是目前最大的开源自负式操纵视频数据集. 我们保留了这些来源的录像和语言描述。

blocks.en: Data preparation. We package all sources in LeRobot 2.1 format. We retain only samples whose videos, language descriptions, and metadata can be linked. We exclude samples with unassociated video, language, or metadata, videos with encoding or decoding failures, and known low-quality samples. Video records retain their corresponding language descriptions and metadata. The inventory counts the recorded episodes and videos at their source durations.
blocks.zh: 数据编制. 我们以 LeRobot 2.1 格式包装所有来源 。 我们只保留其视频、语言描述和元数据可以链接的样本。 我们排除了无关联视频,语言,或元数据样本,有编码或解码故障的视频,以及已知的低质量样本. 视频记录保留了相应的语言描述和元数据. 清点盘点了录制的片段和视频的出处。

blocks.en: Visual content filtering. For general video datasets such as OpenVid and Panda70M, we use original annotations and VLM-based content review to remove animations, static scenes, television programs, and other unsuitable content. For egocentric videos, we use a VLM to assess motion blur, brightness, occlusion, and whether a clip contains meaningful actions, reducing the impact of low-quality imagery and uninformative behavior on training. The UMI and robot demonstrations described below use similar filtering rules.
blocks.zh: 视觉内容过滤. 对于OpenVid和Panda70M等一般视频数据集,我们使用原始说明和基于VLM的内容审查来去除动画,静态场景,电视节目等不合适的内容. 对于以自我为中心的视频,我们用一个VLM来评估运动模糊,亮度,隐蔽性,以及片段是否包含有意义的行动,减少低质量图像和无信息行为对训练的影响. 下面描述的UMI和机器人演示使用类似的过滤规则.

blocks.en: Language annotations describe manipulated objects and executed actions and may additionally include interaction relationships, manipulation processes, and environmental information. For WAM pretraining, what semantic information helps translate video experience into control capabilities? Can these annotations help preserve language–video alignment and improve downstream generalization? We organize language supervision along three dimensions: the level of detail in manipulation descriptions, environmental information, and temporal granularity.
blocks.zh: 语言说明描述了被被操纵的对象和执行的行动,并可能包括互动关系、操纵过程和环境信息。 对于WAM预训,什么语义信息有助于将视频体验转化为控制能力? 这些说明能帮助保留语言-视频对接,改善下游通化吗? 我们围绕三个方面组织语言监督:操纵描述的细节程度、环境信息和时间颗粒性。

blocks.en: Level of detail. Task descriptions cover executed actions, interaction objects, and their attributes during manipulation. We define three levels of descriptive detail, Brief, Medium, and Detailed, with requirements and examples in Table 3 . These levels define controlled language-annotation variants for evaluating how description detail affects the transfer of pretrained video capabilities to robot control.

blocks.en: Scene information. We use Qwen 3.8 Max [ 35 ] and Seed 2.1 Pro [ 36 ] for subtask segmentation and caption annotation. Scene annotations supplement task descriptions with the working environment, spatial layout, and initial state. Lighting annotations describe brightness, exposure, illumination uniformity, and shadows. For example, the scene annotation for one clip is: “The manipulation takes place on a table covered with a black-and-white striped tablecloth, with various packaged snacks scattered across the surface.” Its lighting annotation is: “Indoor lighting is bright and uniform, with no obvious shadows or overexposed regions. All snacks and the manipulation area are clearly visible.”
blocks.zh: 场景资讯. 我们用Quen 3.8 Max [35] 和种子 2.1 Pro [36] 来进行子任务分解和标题注释. 场景说明用工作环境,空间布局,和初始状态来补充任务说明. 照明说明描述出亮度,曝光度,发光的统一性,和阴影. 例如,一个片段的场景注释是:“操纵发生在一张被黑白条纹的桌布覆盖的桌子上,各种包装的小吃散落在地上。” 它的照明说明是:“室内照明光亮而统一,没有明显的阴影或过度暴露的区域。 所有小吃和操纵区都明显可见. “

blocks.en: Temporal granularity. Episode descriptions cover an entire trajectory, while Subtask descriptions correspond to local manipulation segments with start and end times. A VLM segments continuous video into subtasks and outputs each segment’s timestamps and description. Descriptive detail and temporal granularity are independent annotation dimensions: the same subtask can have descriptions at different detail levels, and an entire trajectory can also have a brief or detailed description. During training, the Episode setting uses the description of the full trajectory, while the Subtask setting uses the annotation of the corresponding time interval as the language condition.
blocks.zh: 花期颗粒. Episode描述覆盖了整个轨迹,而Subtask描述则对应有起始和结束时间的局部操纵段. 一个VLM片段连续地录入子任务,输出每个片段的时间戳和描述. 描述性细节和时间颗粒性是独立的注释维度:同样的子任务可以有不同细节级别的描述,而整个轨迹也可以有简短或详细的描述. 在训练期间,Episode设置使用全轨的描述,而Subtask设置则使用相应时间间隔的注释作为语言条件.

blocks.en: 3.3 Language–Video–Action Alignment
blocks.zh: 3.3 语言-视频-行动对接

blocks.en: UMI and robot demonstrations follow the video curation and filtering procedures in Section 3.2.1 and use the language annotations described in Section 3.2.2 . Building on these language–video correspondences, we align video segments with state and action records to construct language–video–action supervision. We describe the collection and curation of these demonstrations below.
blocks.zh: UMI和机器人演示遵循了第3.2.1节中的视频校正和过滤程序,并使用第3.2.2节所描述的语言说明. 根据这些语言-视频通信,我们将视频部分与状态和行动记录相配合,构建语言-视频-行动监督。 下面我们介绍这些示威活动的收集和处理情况。

blocks.en: UMI demonstrations. We use 411,754 in-house UMI trajectories totaling 15,284.9 hours. We collect human manipulation demonstrations using RoboPocket [ 15 ] . The system integrates a smartphone with a handheld adaptive gripper into a portable collection device. Operators interact with objects by moving, opening, and closing the gripper. Its structure and interaction mechanism resemble robot end effectors, reducing interface differences between human demonstrations and robot execution. Our collection tasks include mouse placement, block sorting, seasoning pouring, towel folding, bimanual snack bagging, and other everyday manipulation tasks. They involve pick-and-place, long-horizon manipulation, large wrist rotations, deformable object manipulation, and bimanual coordination. Collection environments include indoor and outdoor scenes with different lighting and background textures.
blocks.zh: UMI示威游行. 我们使用了411 754个内部UMI轨距,共计15 284.9小时。 我们用"机器人"收集人类操纵示威 该系统将带有手持适应性抓取器的智能手机集成到便携式收集设备中. 运算符通过移动,打开和关闭抓取器来与对象交互. 它的结构和相互作用机制类似于机器人端效应器,减少了人类演示和机器人执行之间的界面差异. 我们的收集任务包括鼠标放置,块分拣,调料倒灌,毛巾折叠,双人快餐袋等日常操纵任务. 它们涉及取地和取地,长视距操纵,大腕旋转,可变形物体操纵,以及双相协调. 收藏环境包括室内外景,有不同的照明和背景纹理.

blocks.en: During collection, head and bilateral wrist views record the overall manipulation scene and local interaction details, respectively. Smartphone visual–inertial tracking provides action trajectories, while external encoders record gripper opening and closing. A shared coordinate system and time reference establish spatial and temporal correspondences among the videos of both hands, motion trajectories, and gripper states. The collection procedure includes equipment checks and synchronization verification before recording, tracking stability and kinematic feasibility checks during recording, and video and AR trajectory playback afterward. These checks identify anomalies such as localization drift and trajectory jumps and verify task completion.
blocks.zh: 在收集过程中,头部和双边手腕视图分别记录了总体操纵场景和当地互动细节. 智能手机可视-惰性跟踪提供动作轨迹,而外接编码器则记录了抓取器的开和收. 一个共享的坐标系统和时间参考在双手、运动轨迹和抓取状态的视频之间建立了时空对应关系。 收集程序包括设备检查和同步核查,然后记录、跟踪稳定性和记录过程中的动能可行性检查,以及录相和AR轨迹之后的回放。 这些检查查明了诸如本地化漂移和轨迹跳跃等异常现象并核实任务完成情况.

blocks.en: Robot demonstrations. We curate data from AgiBot World Alpha/Beta/2026 [ 37 ] , RoboCOIN [ 38 ] , RoboMIND [ 39 ] , InternData-A1 [ 40 ] , Galaxea Open-World [ 41 ] , and ABC-130K [ 42 ] . These sources span different robot embodiments, camera configurations, and manipulation environments. We retain only demonstration subsets collected with bimanual robots that include head and bilateral wrist views and meet our quality requirements, maintaining consistent data interfaces and observation semantics. We exclude subsets with missing views, inconsistent view semantics, insufficient image resolution, overly simple tasks, single-arm robot embodiments, or other issues. After applying the configured episode exclusion lists, we retain 768,356 trajectories totaling 9,836.0 hours.
blocks.zh: 机器人演示. 我们整理来自AgiBot World Alpha/Beta/2026 [37],RoboCOIN [38],RoboMIND [39],InternData-A1 [40],Galaxea Open-World [41],以及ABC-130K [42]的数据. 这些来源跨越不同的机器人化身,相机配置,以及操纵环境. 我们只保留了用双人机器人收集的演示子集,包括头部和双边手腕视图,并符合我们的质量要求,保持了一致的数据接口和观测语义. 我们排除了缺少观点、不一致观点语义、图像分辨率不足、任务过于简单、单臂机器人化或其他问题的子集。 在应用了设定的插曲排行榜后,我们保留了768,356个出道时间共计9,836.0小时.

blocks.en: State–action representation. UMI and robot demonstrations use a shared 16-dimensional bimanual end-effector representation. Each hand has a three-dimensional position, a four-dimensional rotation quaternion in wxyz order, and a one-dimensional gripper value. State and action records are associated with their corresponding video segments. Each source is normalized using its own q1 and q99 statistics.
blocks.zh: 国家-行动代表。 UMI和机器人演示使用一个共享的16维双能终极效果表现. 每只手有三维位置,以wxyz顺序为四维旋转之四,并有一维抓取值. 国家记录和行动记录与相应的视频部分有关。 每个来源都使用自己的q1和q99统计数据实现正常化.

blocks.en: Trajectory quality. For our in-house UMI demonstrations, we construct action-supervision masks from the state and action validity annotations provided by the collection pipeline. Videos participate in video learning, while valid action labels additionally provide action supervision and invalid labels are masked. For the collected robot demonstrations, we first check action dimensions, missing values, NaNs, non-finite values, and quaternion validity. For subsets with the required joint and end-effector state fields, we further exclude trajectories with abnormal joint angles, excessive changes in joint angles or end-effector poses between adjacent frames, or no movement throughout the trajectory. Trajectories that pass these quality checks are used for action training.
blocks.zh: 轨迹质量. 为了我们内部的UMI示威活动,我们从收集管道提供的状态和行动有效性说明中制造了行动监督口罩。 视频参与视频学习,而有效的动作标签额外提供动作监督,无效的标签被遮掩. 对于所收集的机器人演示,我们首先检查动作维度,缺失值,NaNs,非无限值,和四元有效性. 对于具有需要的关节和末端效应态域的子集,我们进一步排除了具有异常关节角的轨迹,相邻帧间关节角或末端效应态的过度变化,或者整个轨迹没有运动. 通过这些质量检查的轨迹被用于动作训练.

We also find that many trajectories in the open-source robot data we examine share
the same simple task instruction. Some datasets use task names or short instructions
as video captions, without detailed descriptions of the manipulation process and
environment. For this study, we randomly select nine subsets of the robot data,
containing 145,430 trajectories but only 592 task-level instruction entries. These
shared instructions do not adequately capture differences in manipulation processes
and scene conditions across trajectories, limiting fine-grained correspondence
between language supervision and trajectory-level visual content. We construct two
variants to enrich language supervision. Rephrased provides 100 semantically
equivalent paraphrases per task instruction, randomly sampling one during training to
increase linguistic diversity. Detailed + Env. provides a detailed description of the
specific manipulation process and environment for each trajectory, further enriching
the content and diversity of language supervision. Relative to the 50.80% Hard
success rate of Original, paraphrasing alone yields a gain of 3.96 percentage points,
while Detailed + Env. achieves the highest success rate in this group at 56.16%, as
shown in Table 6 . These results further indicate that
enriching linguistic expression and descriptive content helps improve
language–video alignment and generalization.

blocks.en:
Human manipulation experience provides effective language–video–action supervision. Language–video supervision associates language descriptions with manipulation
processes in videos, while paired action labels further provide supervision for
language–video–action alignment. Direct post-training from Wan achieves a Hard SR of 34.56%.
With robot-data pretraining, it reaches 56.16% in Table 6 ,
demonstrating the value of robot manipulation data. We further examine whether human manipulation experience from UMI
can provide effective cross-embodiment language–video–action supervision. To
examine the contribution of UMI action supervision, we retain all UMI videos and vary
only the proportion of trajectories providing action labels during pretraining.
Videos without action labels continue to participate in video learning. At each
coverage level, the subset of trajectories providing action supervision remains
fixed. All settings use the same pretraining budget, followed by 20k steps of
downstream post-training. From Table 6 , we observe
that as action-label coverage increases from 0% to 100%, the Hard success rate
increases across all five coverage levels, rising from 46.72% to 51.28%, a gain of
4.56 percentage points. These results indicate that paired actions from human
manipulation experience provide effective supervision for robot control, although UMI
data differ visually from robot execution. Given that UMI demonstrations can be
collected with handheld devices across diverse scenes, this finding supports human
manipulation demonstrations as a source for scaling pretraining experience for robot
control.

blocks.en: 4.3 How to integrate multisource experience?

blocks.en:
After examining the roles of language–video and language–video–action supervision, we
study how to integrate multisource experience for pretraining. We first
examine the benefits of increasing training on General videos, egocentric videos,
and UMI demonstrations. Given differences across sources in data quality, scene
and task distributions, and action supervision, we then study how the Ego–UMI
sampling ratio affects downstream control generalization under a fixed
training budget. Finally, we compare model architectures and conditioning
designs under mixed-source training, examining how the pretrained model’s
existing language–video capabilities can support action learning.

blocks.en:
Appropriate architectural choices help preserve pretrained video priors. Under the
same 30k-step multisource pretraining setup, we compare Single-stream, in which video
and actions share a residual stream, with Dual-stream, which maintains
separate residual streams. We also examine the language conditioning pathway
of the action branch. We separate video and action feature spaces to accommodate both the reuse of pretrained video representations and the learning of new action representations. The video branch has already
learned correspondences between language and visual dynamics during
pretraining. The newly introduced text conditioning pathway in the action
branch, however, lacks sufficient pretraining. We therefore aim to reuse the
semantic information available in the video branch for action prediction,
reducing potential interference from the new text conditioning pathway. To
this end, we retain language conditioning in the video branch and let the
action branch access language information only through video features.
As reported in Table 9 , Single-stream and standard
Dual-stream achieve similar Hard success rates of 52.56% and 52.48%,
respectively. The dual-stream model using this language conditioning pathway
achieves the highest Hard success rate in this group at 57.36%, a gain of

conditioning the action branch on language through video features.

blocks.en: 5 Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5. 讨论和结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we studied how to extend pretrained language–video
capabilities to generalizable robot control with multisource experience.
Using approximately 47,000 hours
of experience, we systematically investigated language–video alignment,
language–video–action alignment, and their joint learning.
We found detailed and accurate language descriptions preserve pretrained language–video capabilities.
Meanwhile, action supervision from UMI demonstrations further supports robot control, demonstrating the value of human manipulation experience for robot learning.
Our findings prove the importance of experience organization and supervision usage.
The resulting training recipe demonstrates generalization to unseen conditions in simulation and real-world evaluations, with further gains from continued pretraining.
We release the data, code, and model weights to support future research.
blocks.zh:
在这部作品中,我们研究了如何扩展预训语言-视频
有多种来源经验的通用机器人控制能力。
使用约47 000小时
根据经验,我们系统调查语言 - 视频协调,
语言 - 视频 - 动作对接,以及他们的联合学习。
我们发现详细准确的语言描述保留了预先训练的语言-视频能力。
与此同时,来自UMI演示的动作监督进一步支持了机器人控制,展示了人类操纵经验对机器人学习的价值.
我们的调查结果证明了经验组织和监督使用的重要性。
由此产生的培训方法表明,模拟和现实世界评价普遍到看不见的状况,继续从预先培训中进一步受益。
我们发布数据,代码和模型权重,以支持未来的研究.

blocks.en:
Upon the pretrained video model, the proposed method offers limited support for complex reasoning and explicit multi-stage planning, despite outperforming VLA models in our control generalization evaluations.
The limited historical context may also hinder the execution of long-range tasks.
In the future, we plan to explore memory mechanisms and hierarchical planning to support tasks that require reasoning over past observations and planning subsequent actions.
blocks.zh:
在经过预先训练的视频模型上,拟议的方法对复杂的推理和明确的多阶段规划提供了有限的支持,尽管我们的控制通用评价中VLA模型表现优于.
有限的历史背景还可能妨碍长期任务的执行。
今后,我们计划探索记忆机制和分级规划,以支持需要过去观察推理并规划后续行动的任务.

We use three camera views. Each view is resized to 128 × 160 128\times 160 and arranged into a 2 × \times 2 grid, yielding a final 256 × 320 256\times 320 composite frame. The head-camera view is duplicated across the top row, while the left- and right-wrist views occupy the bottom row. During training, each view is randomly cropped to 95% of its original extent before resizing, followed by color jitter with brightness, contrast, saturation, and hue parameters of 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.08, respectively.
We represent bimanual end-effector states and actions as 16-dimensional vectors and predict actions in chunks of 48 steps.

blocks.en: B.2 Training Configurations
blocks.zh: B.2 培训配置

blocks.en:
In pretraining, we initialize the video DiT from Wan2.2-TI2V-5B [ 2 ] and load its pretrained UMT5-XXL text encoder and Wan2.2 video VAE.
The action branch, including the action and state encoders, transformer blocks, and action decoder, is randomly initialized.
For each experiment, post-training starts from the corresponding pretrained weights.
blocks.zh:
在预训中,我们从Wan2.2-TI2V-5B[2]初始化了视频DiT,并装入其预训的UMT5-XXL文本编码器和Wan2.2视频VAE.
动作分支,包括动作和状态编码器,变压器块,和动作解码器,是随机初始化的.
对于每个实验,后训练从相应的预训练重量开始.

blocks.en:
Training uses BF16 mixed precision.
The default global batch size for ablation studies is 256.
We increase it to 512 for pretraining in the scaling study and subsequent robot-data pretraining described in Section 4.4 , as well as for pretraining the final models evaluated in Section 4.5 .
For the scaling study, we sample egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations with equal probability and use detailed subtask descriptions with scene and lighting information.
We evaluate checkpoints at 25k, 50k, 75k, and 100k steps, as shown in Figure 5 .
Table 13 compares pretraining in the scaling study with simulation and real-world post-training.
blocks.zh:
训练使用BF16混合精度.
衰减研究的默认全球批量大小为256.
我们将其增加到512个,用于第4.4节所述的缩放研究和随后机器人数据预训的预训,以及第4.5节所评价的最后模型的预训。
对于缩放研究,我们以同样概率对以自我为中心的视频和UMI演示进行取样,并使用带有场景和照明信息的详细子任务描述.
如图5所示,我们评价25克、50克、75克和100克的检查站。
表13将缩放研究中的预训与模拟和现实世界后培训进行比较。

blocks.en:
We jointly train a single model on all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks using 50 Clean demonstrations per task, following the same post-training protocol across simulation experiments.
Each sample contains left-wrist, right-wrist, and head-camera views and the current bimanual end-effector state. The same three-view preprocessing and augmentation settings described above are used during simulation post-training.
We use absolute end-effector states and actions and normalize both with their q99 statistics.
blocks.zh:
我们联合训练一个单一的模型 用于所有50个RoboTwin 2.0任务 使用50个清洁演示, 遵循同样的训练后协议 通过模拟实验。
每个样本都包含左手腕,右手腕,和头相机的视角以及目前的双人终极效应状态. 在模拟后训练中使用上述相同的三视预处理和增强设置.
我们使用绝对的终极效应状态和行动,使其与q99统计正常化。

We apply this procedure to cup stacking, towel folding, and gift-in-box.

blocks.en:
We use a bimanual Flexiv Rizon 4 platform.
Observations comprise two fisheye wrist-camera views and one fixed head-camera view.
Actions encode the end-effector position, orientation, and continuous gripper width for each arm.
For OpenWAM, we follow its official default configuration and use a 6D rotation representation.
All other models represent orientation with a wxyz quaternion, yielding a 16-dimensional action vector across both arms.

我们使用双人Flexiv Rizon 4平台.
观察包括两个鱼眼手腕-相机视图和一个固定头-相机视图。
动作编码每个臂的末端效果器位置,取向和连续抓取宽度.
对于OpenWAM,我们遵循其官方默认配置,并使用6D旋转代表.
所有其他模型都以wxyz之四为取向,使双臂都有16维的动作矢量。

blocks.en: C.2 Evaluation Protocols and Metrics
blocks.zh: C.2 评价议定书和计量

blocks.en:
We evaluate under Easy (C2C) and Hard (C2R) settings.
Easy settings retain the scene conditions and physical objects used in post-training, including their shapes and colors, while varying their initial configurations across layouts.
Hard settings vary across scene and object attributes, including background, tabletop material, object instance, shape, color, size, and texture.
The evaluation layouts are illustrated in Figure 9 .
All models use synchronous inference and execute actions at 30 Hz.
blocks.zh:
我们在Easy(C2C)和Hard(C2R)设置下进行评估.
轻松的设置保留了训练后使用的场景条件和实物,包括其形状和颜色,同时在布局上各有不同的初始配置.
硬度设置因场景和对象属性而异,包括背景,平面材料,对象实例,形状,颜色,大小,以及纹理等.
图9说明了评价的布局。
所有模型都使用同步推论,并在30Hz执行动作.

blocks.en:
A layout specifies the initial object configurations, target positions, and scene appearance.
For each task and setting, ten layouts are fixed before evaluation and shared across all models.
We run three trials per layout to account for variability in object placement and model sampling, yielding 30 trials per task and setting.
To reproduce a layout, we align the fixed live head-camera view with a reference photograph using an image overlay.
blocks.zh:
一个布局指定了初始对象配置,目标位置,和场景外观.
对于每项任务和设定,在评价前确定10个布局,并在所有模型中共享.
我们每个布局进行三次试验,以考虑到物体布置和模型取样的可变性,每次任务和布置进行30次试验。
为了复制布局,我们把固定的活头-相机视图与使用图像覆盖的参考相片相接.

blocks.en:
Each task is divided into predefined, equally weighted subtasks, scored by reviewing execution videos.
The protocol permits up to five additional autonomous replanning attempts after an initial failed attempt, retaining the current environment state and execution history without human assistance.
All models follow the same retry and termination rules.
A trial is marked as a failure if the cup tower collapses or an object leaves the workspace.
blocks.zh:
每个任务被分为预先定义的,同样加权的子任务,通过审查执行视频来打分.
议定书允许在一次初步失败的尝试后再进行多达五次自主的重新规划,在没有人力援助的情况下保留目前的环境状况和执行历史。
所有型号都遵循同样的重试和终止规则.
如果杯子塔倒塌或物体离开工作空间,试验被标记为失败.

Figure 10 shows the three real-world tasks and their corresponding ordered subtask decompositions.
Cup stacking requires arranging cups into a stable pyramid, towel folding requires folding a towel in half twice, and gift-in-box requires placing a gift inside an open gift box.
We divide these tasks into seven, four, and two subtasks, respectively, corresponding to observable milestones in task execution.
These decompositions define the task-specific subtask counts K K used in the PSR calculation above.
blocks.zh:
图10显示了三个现实世界的任务及其相应的被命令的子任务分解.
杯子堆放需要将杯子安排入一个稳定的金字塔,毛巾折叠需要将毛巾折叠成相隔了半个半个,而"礼物入盒"则需要将礼物放入一个开放的礼品盒.
我们将这些任务分别分为7个、4个和2个子任务,与任务执行中可观察到的里程碑相对应。
这些分解定义了以上PSR计算中使用的任务特定子任务计数K K.
